chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

Three men were brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. One of them had restrained a man, then another came and killed him, while the other was watching them. So he ruled concerning the lookout that his eyes be put out, concerning the one who restrained him that he be imprisoned until he dies just as he had restrained, and he ruled concerning the one who killed that he be killed.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the Commander of the Faithful, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, acting here as judge
key_terms.أَمْسَكَ: restrained or held the victim so the killing could occur
key_terms.الرَّبِيئَةِ: the lookout or watcher who observed and assisted indirectly
key_terms.تُسْمَلَ عَيْنَاهُ: that his eyes be put out as the assigned punishment
key_terms.يُقْتَلَ: that he be put to death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when several people participate in a murder by killing, restraining, and acting as a lookout?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding joint participation in a killing through direct killing, restraint, and lookout. It shows differentiated punishment according to each participant’s role in the murder and reflects principles of criminal liability in Shia fiqh.
